variants.headline: New settlers land from the ship
variants.sub: The ship in port has brought new settlers who landed at {district}.
variants.body:
New settlers have landed from the ship at {district}. The number arriving is {migrants}. Their arrival is an entry into the colony, not a complete account of the lives that follow. For {target}, the relevant question concerns responsibility towards newcomers as people rather than merely an addition to a count.

New settlers are people, not merely potential labour. Work matters, and so does the life a person is trying to make. Labour should insist on that full perspective when an arrival is discussed, without inventing either a job waiting for someone or a hardship the report does not describe.

We judge {target} critically. A landing should not place the treatment of newcomers beyond question; people joining the colony deserve a more serious standard than a welcoming description with practical responsibility left outside it. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
